message:
Hello Alex Johnson, I am Noah, an AI interviewer.

This conversation will take about 20 minutes. The goal is to get a deep understanding of your work, your role, expertise, daily tasks, the tools you use, any challenges you face, and your ambitions for the future.
Before we begin, could you let me know in which language you would like to do this interview? You can choose Dutch, French, German, or English.
English works for me.

Perfect, we'll conduct the entire interview in English.

Let's start with the basics — could you tell me what your job title is and what your role involves?

I'm a Computer Repair Technician at TechFix Solutions. My role involves diagnosing and repairing both hardware and software issues on computers. I also provide repair cost calculations at the end of the process.
That's clear, thank you. Can you walk me through what a typical day looks like for you — what tasks do you actually spend your time on?

Sure, a typical day starts with checking any new repair requests that have come in. I spend a lot of time diagnosing issues, either through hardware checks or software configuration, depending on the problem. After repairs, I run system functionality tests, and then I calculate the repair costs. If there are any issues with parts or the billing system, I handle those too.
Got it. When you say you spend a lot of time diagnosing — roughly how many hours per day would you say you dedicate to that, and how many repair jobs do you typically handle?
I spend around 2 to 3 hours diagnosing issues each day, depending on the complexity. On average, I handle about 3 to 5 repair jobs daily.
That's helpful. And after diagnosis, when you move into the actual repair and testing phase, how long does that typically take per job?
After diagnosis, the repair and testing phase usually takes about 1.5 to 2 hours per job. It can vary depending on the specific issues I encounter.
Makes sense. So you're spending roughly 5 to 7 hours on diagnosis, repair, and testing combined — what about the cost calculations you mentioned, how much time does that take daily?
Cost calculations take about 15 to 20 minutes per job. So, depending on the number of repairs, it can add up to about 1 to 1.5 hours a day.
Thank you for quantifying that. Now I'm curious — what knowledge or expertise do you bring to this role that helps you stand out, and what parts of your work feel most natural or energising to you?

I've got a strong background in both hardware and software repair, which helps me diagnose complex issues effectively. I really enjoy the challenge of solving difficult technical problems, and I find working with new technologies energizing. My customer service skills also help me communicate well with clients, which is important in this role.
That's great. When you're solving those complex technical problems, what would you say are your strongest areas — is it more on the hardware side, software side, or are you equally strong in both?
I'd say I'm equally strong in both hardware and software. I have a good eye for detail, which helps when diagnosing issues in either area.
Excellent. Now let's talk about how you work with others — how does cooperation work internally with your team, and are there any bottlenecks in how you collaborate?

We collaborate pretty well as a team, especially when diagnosing tough problems or when parts aren't available. A bottleneck can occur if we’re waiting for hardware components to arrive, which delays repairs. In those cases, we keep the customer informed and manage expectations together.
That makes sense. When you're waiting for parts, how often does that happen, and roughly how much work time does it cost you per week?
It happens occasionally, maybe once or twice a week. It doesn't cost much work time on my end since I can shift focus to other repairs, but it does delay the completion of the affected job.
Got it. Beyond parts delays, are there other frustrations or bottlenecks in your daily work — things that feel inefficient or annoying?
Sometimes the billing software can be a bit glitchy, which affects cost estimation. When that happens, I have to manually calculate the costs and update the system, which can be a bit time-consuming.
How often does the billing software glitch, and roughly how much extra time does that manual calculation add to your day when it happens?
The billing software glitches aren't super frequent, maybe a couple of times a month. When it does happen, it can add about 20 to 30 minutes to my day.
Understood. Besides the billing software issues, what else slows you down or feels like unnecessary steps in your workflow?
Honestly, besides the occasional software glitch and waiting for parts, my workflow is usually pretty smooth. There's not much else that feels unnecessary.
That's good to hear. Let me ask — are there any tasks that lead to errors or rework, or times when you have to redo something?

Not often, but if a hardware component fails after installation or there's a miscommunication about a repair, it can lead to rework. We do our best to double-check everything to prevent those situations.
When those rework situations happen, how often would you say that occurs, and what's usually the main cause — is it the component failure or the miscommunication?
It doesn't happen very often, maybe once a month. It's usually more about component failure rather than miscommunication. Components can be unpredictable at times.
Fair enough. Now, thinking about your future — how do you see your role evolving, and what would you like to spend more time on?

I'd like to spend more time learning about emerging technologies and possibly move into a more specialized role, like network security or advanced diagnostics. I'm always eager to expand my skill set and take on new challenges.
That's interesting. If you could change or improve one thing about your current workflow, what would it be?
I'd probably want to streamline the billing process a bit more, maybe with more reliable software, to save time and reduce errors. That would make things more efficient overall.

That's a clear priority. Beyond billing, is there anything else in your workflow you'd like to automate or have assistance with — whether it's the diagnostics, testing, documentation, or something else?
Automating some parts of the diagnostics could be helpful, like having more advanced tools that can quickly identify issues. It would speed up the process and allow for more accurate results.
That makes sense. When you're doing diagnostics now, what specific steps or checks feel most repetitive or time-consuming that could potentially be automated?

Running initial hardware checks can be pretty repetitive, especially when dealing with the same types of issues. Automating those basic diagnostics could save time and let me focus on more complex problems.

Perfect. So to recap what we've covered — I have a clear picture of your role, your typical day with time breakdowns, your strengths, the collaboration dynamics, and your main pain points around billing software and repetitive diagnostics. I think we've now covered all the important topics for this discovery conversation.

Thank you so much for your time and thoughtful answers, Alex — this has been really valuable. You can now press the red button to end the conversation.
Sure, glad I could help.
Great! Thanks again for your openness and detailed responses. Press the red button whenever you're ready to end the session.
